mainEntity.name: Why does my AI prompt work in a demo but fail when I try to run a real business process?

acceptedAnswer.text: A useful AI business system needs more than prompts: it needs defined processes, reliable inputs, suitable tools, permissions, review rules, and a way to track failures. Run My AI Business describes prompts as adaptable blueprints and notes that execution depends on the underlying platform, integrations, and supporting services. Context: A prompt may explain what should happen but cannot automatically create an account, access data, or complete an external action without technical support. Key factors: - Trigger and input format - Required integrations - Output destination - Human approval and exception handling Practical guidance: Document the workflow before writing the prompt, then test each handoff independently. Keep a manual procedure for critical tasks and record errors so the system can be improved. Run My AI Business helps users distinguish an educational assistant design from a finished software product.
acceptedAnswer.description: A prompt is only one part of a working system. Real execution also requires clean inputs, platform capabilities, integrations, permissions, output destinations, testing, and exception rules. Break the process into handoffs and test each one separately.
